newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korean farm facilities damaged - FAO chief.
newsitem.headline: North Korean farm facilities damaged - FAO chief.

text.p: North Korea's agricultural infrastructure, devastated by floods, needs to be improved to solve the food shortages there, according to the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organisation's (FAO) head.
"North Korea's problem is that its irrigation system and the roads used to transport crops were destroyed by floods," FAO director-general Jacques Diouf told Reuters in a weekend interview in Tokyo.

"We have to think about short-term measures first, such as sending food aid. But for the long term, North Korea needs to improve its water control, crop transport system and fertiliser supplies," said Diouf, who was in Tokyo to open an FAO office.
Stalinist North Korea was hit by massive flooding in 1995 and 1996 which led to the devastation of cereal crops across the country.
The World Food Programme (WFP), the U.N. agency which plans emergency food aid distribution, cautioned after a visit last month that North Korea was within months of running out of food supplies.
On June 30, the Rome-based FAO said that 50,000 tonnes of fertiliser costing some $11 million were needed for distribution in North Korea over the next six weeks.

While in Tokyo, Diouf signed an agreement to open FAO's Japan office and met with government ministers, including the ministers of foreign affairs and agriculture. But he said he did not raise the food aid issue during the meetings with the ministers.
Diouf, who left Tokyo on Sunday, also called for the Japanese government to step up its commitment to the global food issue and play a role as a coordinator among the FAO's members.
